clue.text: The water-chute's dry counterpart?

parts.note: a water-chute is a water slide; the same kind of slide on dry ground rather than water is the collapse of a hillside

explanation.surface: A question about what a playground water-chute would be without the water.
explanation.walkthrough: A water-chute is a water slide, so its dry counterpart is a slide of earth: a fall of soil and rock down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry-ground slide is a mass of earth and rock slipping down a hillside, the opposite of a slide into water.

clue.text: Banker giving Florence the go-by

parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river (it has banks); this one flows past the Tuscan city of Florence

explanation.surface: A financier who snubs a woman called Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' looks like a money man and Florence like a woman's name; in crosswords a banker is a river, and this river runs past the city of Florence in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan river flowing through the city of Florence on its way to Pisa and the sea.

clue.text: Dingy church with a place in modern history

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown, a dingy colour
kirk is the Scottish word for a church

explanation.surface: A drab little church that once played a part in recent history.
explanation.walkthrough: The French port is famous for the 1940 evacuation of British troops, hence 'a place in modern history'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French port where Allied troops were evacuated by sea in 1940, a landmark of twentieth-century history.

clue.text: Put on a pound and make light of it

definitions.text: Put on a pound and make light of it

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra
to ignite something is to set it alight

explanation.surface: Advice to gain weight and laugh it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: brown coal is put on the fire and then set alight. 'Put on a pound' reads as gaining weight and 'make light of' as shrugging off.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown coal is a fuel shovelled onto a fire and then kindled, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Lady made an amendment

indicators.note: an amendment is a change, so the letters of the word made are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman makes a correction to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame is a title for a woman of rank, a synonym of lady.

clue.text: Particular transport causing a stir in places

indicators.note: the transport is what the letters of a stir in places cause when rearranged, so causing signals the anagram

explanation.surface: Some special mode of travel stirs up trouble in various parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' turns the thirteen letters of A STIR IN PLACES into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trains laid on for a particular purpose or occasion are particular forms of transport.

clue.text: There's a moral difference between them

definitions.text: There's a moral difference between them

parts.words: There's a moral difference between them
parts.note: the pair of opposites that ethics separates: what is good conduct and what is bad

explanation.surface: A remark that two things differ in ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: Good and bad conduct are the two things distinguished by morality, so the difference between them is moral.

clue.text: Tricky move for a start on board

definitions.text: Tricky move for a start on board

parts.words: Tricky move for a start on board
parts.note: a crafty first move at the chessboard, often sacrificing a piece; also any first ploy in a negotiation

explanation.surface: A cunning first step for someone joining a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship or a boardroom; the board is a chessboard and the move is a chess opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess term for a first move offering a sacrifice to gain an advantage, a tricky start.

clue.text: Aid to light concentration

parts.note: a cover that focuses a bulb's glow downward, read as helping light to concentrate rather than helping someone concentrate a little

explanation.surface: Something that helps with mild focus of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light concentration' reads as gentle mental focus; it means concentrating light, which a shade round a bulb does.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade round a bulb directs and concentrates its glow in one direction.

clue.text: Element Agnes and I keep 0 mum about

indicators.note: the word mum goes about, or around, the other pieces, so it is the container here

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Agnes and I stay silent about a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep mum' looks like 'stay quiet'; here MUM is placed about AGNES and I, giving M + AGNESI + UM. The '0' is a stray mark in the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A light silvery metal, number twelve in the periodic table, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Designing part of the foot

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means cunning or crafty, as in a designing schemer
the curved underside of the foot between heel and ball

explanation.definitionFit: Arch means crafty or scheming, and is also the curved section of the sole between heel and toes.

clue.text: Small creature, one of a number in a pie

indicators.note: the other pieces are put in the pie, so in marks the container

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
X is the Roman numeral ten, a number

explanation.surface: A tiny animal, one of many baked inside a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls blackbirds baked in a pie; the pieces I and X go inside PIE, after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous fairy of folklore, a little supernatural being.

clue.text: Goddess changing her to a bird .

definitions.meaning: a Titaness of Greek myth, mother of Zeus
a large flightless South American bird like a small ostrich

explanation.surface: A goddess transforms a woman into a bird, as in myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing her to a' is not needed for the meaning: rearranging HER and adding A spells the same name, so the goddess's name is the bird's.
explanation.definitionFit: A Titaness of Greek myth shares her name with a flightless South American bird.

clue.text: A fine coffee to imitate, one hears

indicators.note: says the pieces are taken by their sound when spoken, not their spelling

parts.note: to mock is to imitate, often in ridicule
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good coffee that someone hears is a copy of another.
explanation.walkthrough: MOCK is spoken and written MOCH, with A from the clue's first word added at the end; said together they give the coffee's name. 'one hears' signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-quality Arabian coffee named after the Yemeni port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Romantic club?

definitions.meaning: to kiss and cuddle, behave romantically
an old wooden golf club with a lofted face

explanation.definitionFit: To spoon is old slang for courting amorously, and it was also an old lofted golf club.

clue.text: … not a fantail, though it struts with one

definitions.text: not a fantail, though it struts with one

parts.words: not a fantail, though it struts with one
parts.note: a fantail is a kind of pigeon; this proud bird is no pigeon, yet parades with a fanned-out tail

explanation.surface: A bird that is no fancy pigeon still shows off a fanned tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue follows on from the one before with dots. A fantail is a breed of pigeon; the bird meant shows off a tail spread like a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: The male peafowl displays a huge fanned train while strutting, though it is not the fantail pigeon.

clue.text: Account for a broken axle-pin

indicators.note: a broken axle-pin is in pieces, so its letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone must justify a snapped part of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give the reasons for it, to make it clear.

clue.text: Hold-up in a Hertfordshire town

parts.note: a hitch is a delay or snag, a hold-up
taken as written

explanation.surface: A delay somewhere in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is an English county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in north Hertfordshire, England.

clue.text: Sounded as if the horse made an objection

definitions.text: Sounded as if the horse made an objection

parts.words: Sounded as if the horse made an objection
parts.note: a horse's call sounds like saying nay, which is objecting

explanation.surface: A horse protesting with a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The horse's noise sounds the same as 'nayed', said no.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's whinny is spelt like that noise but sounds like the word for saying no.

clue.text: Male preferences? Fair enough

parts.note: fair-haired women are the preference, and fair means light-haired

explanation.surface: Granting that men have their tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays on the film and novel 'Gentlemen Prefer Blondes'; 'Fair enough' looks like a shrug but means fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair-haired women, said in the famous title to be what gentlemen prefer.

clue.text: Withdraw with a slipped disc?

definitions.meaning: to pull out of a commitment
an injured spine read literally: the back is out

explanation.definitionFit: To pull out of a deal; read literally, a slipped disc leaves your spine out of place.

clue.text: Anything but a singular doctrinal link with 7

definitions.text: Anything but a singular doctrinal link with 7

parts.words: Anything but a singular doctrinal link with 7
parts.note: in grammar the number for two, not singular; also the doctrine linking good and evil as twin opposites, as in 7 down

explanation.surface: A doctrine connected to a moral pair.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar a word for exactly two is the opposite of singular; the doctrine of two opposing forces ties in with 7 down, the moral pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-fold, as opposed to singular, and the name of a belief in two opposed principles such as good and evil.

clue.text: However you hear it, in honesty you shouldn't

definitions.text: However you hear it, in honesty you shouldn't

parts.words: However you hear it, in honesty you shouldn't
parts.note: the first letter of honesty is silent, so the letter's name should never be heard in that word

explanation.surface: Advice that, honestly, one shouldn't listen whatever one hears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in honesty' looks like 'honestly'; it means inside the word honesty, whose first letter is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the letter H, which is silent at the start of honesty.

clue.text: The language at Cockney girl's party?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the h of words, so her do becomes er do

parts.note: her do, a do being a party

explanation.surface: Which tongue is spoken at a London girl's party?
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent drops the H, so 'her do' (her party) is said 'er do'.
explanation.definitionFit: The official language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: A pound to an old penny one's. in next to nothing here

definitions.text: A pound to an old penny one's. in next to nothing here

indicators.note: the last piece sits next to, just after, what comes before
one is placed in the pound and penny pair, so in marks the insertion

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound
d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money
I is the Roman numeral for one
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Odds of a pound to a penny that you'd wear almost nothing here.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: at an open-air pool one wears next to nothing. Before 1971, British pennies were written d.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air public swimming pool, where bathers wear only swimsuits.

clue.text: Sweet for an aficionado about fifty

indicators.note: the fan goes about, around, the letter for fifty

parts.note: a fan is an aficionado, an enthusiast
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A dessert for an enthusiast aged around fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: An open pastry tart, often a dessert, is a sweet course.

clue.text: When the coast is clear, presumably

definitions.text: When the coast is clear, presumably

parts.words: When the coast is clear, presumably
parts.note: taken literally, when a shoreline can be seen plainly from a ship rather than the idiom for no one watching

explanation.surface: When nobody is around to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the coast is clear' is the idiom for no one watching; read literally it means the shore is visible from sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors near enough to see the shore can see the coast clearly.

clue.text: Pack a gem it's quite attractive

parts.note: to load is to pack goods in
a precious stone is a gem

explanation.surface: Wrap up a jewel, as it is very pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attractive' reads as pretty; it means magnetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturally magnetic iron ore that attracts iron.
